extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in nonlinear dynamics/time-series analysis applying recurrence plots (RPs) and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) to temporal and spatial data (including synchronization analysis)
extracted.subtask_description: Methods, definitions and evaluation criteria for constructing and quantifying recurrence plots (temporal and spatial), and for detecting types/onsets of synchronisation (phase, generalised, lag) using recurrence-based indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding-parameter invariance of p_c(m,τ)(ε,l)
rubrics_metrics.description: p(m,τ)_c(ε,l) = p(m',τ')_c(ε,l') if l + (m−1)τ = l' + (m'−1)τ', provided l,l' > τ,τ' (so the curve is only shifted when dimension is decreased).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relationship implies that the estimate of K2 based on the slope of ln p(m,τ)_c(ε,l) for large l is independent of the choice of embedding parameters, because curves for different embeddings are shifted versions of each other when the above equality holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of D2 estimation via RPs from embedding parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The estimation of D2 by means of recurrence plots (RPs) is independent of the choice of embedding parameters (derived from substitution in Eq. (79) / Eq. (104)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an advantage of RP-based methods compared to others — practitioners may vary embedding parameters without affecting the D2 estimate, as long as conditions analogous to the p_c invariance hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial recurrence plot (RP) definition and dimensionality
rubrics_metrics.description: For d-dimensional Cartesian space: R_{ĩ,ĵ} = Θ(ε - ||x_ĩ - x_ĵ||), where ĩ and ĵ are d-dimensional coordinates and x_ĩ the phase-space vector at location ĩ; the resulting RP has dimension 2d and cannot be visualised directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret each spatial direction as an embedding vector of dimension m and compare each with all others; quantification is still possible even when visualization is infeasible due to high dimensionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyper-surface of identity (HSOI) in spatial RPs
rubrics_metrics.description: The HSOI is the d-dimensional diagonal-oriented structure (generalisation of LOI) in the 2d-dimensional spatial RP defined by R_{ĩ,ĩ} ≡ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In special cases (e.g., 2D image with scalar values, m=1) the RP is 4D and HSOI is a 2D plane. Use HSOI concept when defining diagonal/vertical hyper-surfaces and computing RQA for spatial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonal hyper-surface and vertical hyper-surface definitions for spatial RPs
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagonal hyper-surface of size l (~l = (l,...,l)) is defined by the product over k1,...,kd of R_{ĩ+k,ĵ+k} = 1 (Eq. (108)); a vertical hyper-surface of size v (~v = (v,...,v)) is defined analogously (Eq. (109)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to compute frequency distributions of sizes of diagonal and vertical hyper-surfaces in spatial RPs and then apply RQA measures (as defined for 1D) to these distributions to characterise spatial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of RP structures (points, extended structures, periodic patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single points correspond to strongly fluctuating, uncorrelated data (noise). Correlations cause extended structures (lines, planes, cuboids). Periodic recurrent patterns induce periodic lines/planes in the RP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these qualitative interpretations when diagnosing the observed RP: e.g., random image → mostly single-point RP; correlated or AR processes → extended structures; periodic structures → repeating diagonal/planar patterns (illustrated by examples A,B,C and corresponding RP slices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence quantification measures applied to spatial RPs (RR, DET, LAM, DETHS, LAMHS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard RQA measures (recurrence rate RR, determinism DET, laminarity LAM) can be computed on frequency distributions of diagonal/vertical hyper-surfaces for spatial RPs; for spatial-specific labels DETHS and LAMHS denote determinism and laminarity of hyper-surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: with images normalised to same SD, RR is roughly the same across examples; noise yields DETHS≈0 and LAMHS≈0; AR2 shows small positive DETHS and LAMHS indicating local correlations; periodic images yield high DETHS and LAMHS. Interpret DETHS as probability that similar changes recur; LAMHS as probability that a specific value remains unchanged over spatial variation (extended same-colour areas). Minimal sizes (e.g., l_min=3, v_min=4) are used to exclude trivial short structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of joint recurrence plots (JRPs) and joint R´enyi entropy (JK2) for synchronisation detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate JK2 from JRPs to characterise transitions to phase synchronisation (PS) and lag synchronisation (LS); JK2 plotted over parameter space (e.g., frequency mismatch ν and coupling µ) reveals structure such as Arnold tongues and fine details not seen in simple mean-frequency difference ∆Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JK2 is computed from time series JRPs and is robust even when model equations are unknown. JK2 is bounded above by the sum of positive Lyapunov exponents of the whole system; differences vs Lyapunov-based diagnostics can reveal complementary information (e.g., JK2 distinguishes the tip of Arnold tongue better in some parameter ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation of recurrence probability p(ε,τ) via diagonal-wise τ-recurrence rate RR_τ
rubrics_metrics.description: p̂(ε,τ) = RR_τ(ε) = (1/(N−τ)) Σ_{i=1}^{N−τ} Θ(ε − ||x_i − x_{i+τ}||) (Eq. (111)); treat p̂(ε,τ) as a generalised auto-correlation function revealing τ-dependent correlations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the diagonal-wise computed RR_τ to obtain p(τ) (shorthand). Compare p(τ) between coupled systems to identify coinciding maxima (same time scales) as evidence for PS.

rubrics_metrics.name: CP_R index for phase synchronisation (PS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CP_R is the correlation coefficient between p_x(τ) and p_y(τ), where p's are normalised to zero mean and unit std: CP_R = ⟨ p̄_x(τ) p̄_y(τ) ⟩ (Eq. (112)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CP_R ≈ 1 the systems are in PS (maxima of p(τ) coincide); small CP_R indicates non-PS. CP_R is robust to noise, and simulations show near-independence from the choice of threshold ε provided both RPs have the same percentage of black points (recommended: matching black point percentage between 1% and 90%). Examples: CP_R=0.998 for PS Rössler example, CP_R≈0.115 when not PS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase estimation approaches and their applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system has a dominant spectral peak, project trajectory onto an appropriate plane and define phase Φ(t)=arctan(y(t)/x(t)) (Eq. (110)) — works when projection shows rotations around an origin; alternative curvature-based phase exists for non-coherent regimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveats: projection-based phase fails for non-phase-coherent signals (no clear center); curvature-based methods are limited to low-dimensional systems and sensitive to noise. Ensemble-of-oscillators filtering is another approach but results may depend on which coordinate is coupled to the ensemble.

rubrics_metrics.name: JP_R index for generalised synchronisation (GS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define S(τ)= RR_{x,y}(τ) / RR (using JRPs computed with FAN); then JP_R = normalised max_τ S(τ) giving a value in [0,1] that ranges from ~0 for independence to ~1 for GS (Eqs. (113),(114)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FAN (fixed number of nearest neighbours N_n per column) to compute recurrence matrices when attractor shapes differ; set RR = N_n / N. JP_R is rather independent of RR choice in practice. Examples: driven Lorenz/Rössler GS yields JP_R≈0.64 (RR=0.02), independent systems yield JP_R≈0.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FAN (fixed amount of nearest neighbours) vs fixed threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems with essentially different attractor shapes that undergo GS, it is more appropriate to use FAN (fixed N_n) rather than fixed distance thresholds; FAN corresponds to original RP definition by Eckmann et al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With FAN, RR_x = RR_y = N_n/N is fixed and comparable across subsystems; this avoids misleading joint recurrence measures that arise when using identical distance thresholds on different-shaped attractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages and limitations of recurrence-based synchronisation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrence-based methods can detect PS and GS from time series (even noisy and non-phase-coherent) where other methods fail; they rely on marginal and joint recurrence probabilities rather than nearest-neighbour distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare with alternatives: conditional stability (requires Lyapunov estimation), auxiliary system (requires identical copy), MFNN (problems with multiple time scales), δp/δp,q and auxiliary-system time-series implementations solve some issues. Recurrence approach is comparable computationally (O(N^2)) and can handle non-invertibility/wrinkling by increasing embedding dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Lyapunov spectrum and validation of synchronisation indices
rubrics_metrics.description: For coupled systems considered as a single system, JK2 relates to the sum of positive Lyapunov exponents (JK2 ≤ Σ_{λ_i>0} λ_i). Onset of PS is associated with a zero Lyapunov exponent becoming negative (e.g., λ4 < 0 indicates PS); onset of LS associated with further Lyapunov crossings (e.g., λ2 crossing zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recurrence-based indices (CP_R, JP_R, JK2) alongside Lyapunov-spectrum diagnostics when equations are known to validate onsets and transitions; note that exact equalities like K2 = sum λ_i hold only for hyperbolic systems, so differences can be expected for non-hyperbolic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diagonal-line distances and their distributions to infer time scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal lines in an RP reflect determinism; the vertical distances between diagonal lines correspond to characteristic time scales of the system; chaotic dynamics yield interrupted diagonal lines with a distribution of distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect PS by comparing positions of maxima in p(τ) (i.e., matching dominant recurrence lags); matching maxima implies phase/frequency locking even when amplitudes differ (PS without GS/CS). Use RR_τ to obtain these distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical parameter/rule-of-thumb choices and robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples give practical defaults: minimal diagonal plane size l_min = 3 and v_min = 4 used in spatial RQA examples; choice of ε should produce comparable recurrence densities across compared RPs (match percentage of black points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CP_R outcomes are robust for ε choices giving 1%–90% black points when matched between systems. JP_R is rather independent of RR. When computing JRPs for GS detection, prefer FAN (fixed N_n) to ensure RR equality across subsystems.
